scores.evidence: On POSIX systems `os.rename` replaces an existing target without warning, and on case-insensitive file systems `IMG_1.JPG` and `img_1.jpg` count as the same name
scores.rationale: All technical claims check out, including the subtle ones: POSIX rename semantics, case-insensitive filesystems, link+unlink no-clobber, QuickTime CreateDate in UTC, and correct exiftool syntax.

scores.evidence: preview by default, a journal with one-command undo, collision handling that is safe on case-insensitive file systems, and sidecar files kept with their photos
scores.rationale: Solves exactly the stated problem, resolves ambiguities (formats, timezones, videos) explicitly, is trivially buildable by one developer, and justifies every exclusion in §10.

scores.evidence: pure Python (Pillow plus `pillow-heif`) behind a `DateSource` interface. If V2 fails, switch to PyExifTool for the failing formats
scores.rationale: Components, phases, decisions and validation gates all reference each other consistently; the no-overwrite and journal choices made in §3 are honored in every later section with no contradiction.

scores.evidence: Across ≥ 10,000 cases per file system and ≥ 200 kills: the set of file hashes is identical before and after apply
scores.rationale: Validation is built around the actual failure risks (overwrite, crash mid-run, wrong dates), uses property-based tests, fault injection and an exiftool reference oracle, with checkable thresholds labeled as assumptions and gating before originals are touched.

scores.evidence: ASSUMPTION (basis: renaming must never destroy content; confirm you never want overwrite mode)
scores.rationale: Every number and constraint is explicitly labeled with its basis, unknowns are listed with how they will be resolved, and each key assumption has a stated revisit trigger describing what changes if it is wrong.

scores.evidence: kill the process at a random rename index, then `undo` or `resume`... an injected truncated JPEG and an injected read-only file each show up as a reported error
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures concretely: silent overwrite, crash mid-run with intent/done journal recovery, malformed and malicious EXIF (path injection), case-collision, partial failure isolation, and parser vulnerabilities via pip-audit.

scores.evidence: install the previous release wheel with pipx and confirm with `--version`. On the data side, `undo`
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback (both code and data), logging, exit codes, run IDs and journal version compatibility are all specified and sized correctly to a one-developer CLI.

scores.evidence: you may not need to build this. `exiftool '-FileName<DateTimeOriginal' ...` already covers a one-off job
scores.rationale: Build-vs-buy is reasoned explicitly, run cost is zero by design, and resource budgets are stated, but the dominant cost (engineering time to build the phases) is never estimated even roughly.

scores.evidence: R2. It would be R3 without the seam, because an overwrite is permanent; the preview, journal, and no-clobber seam is built in Phase 0
scores.rationale: Explicitly rates reversibility of each decision, isolates the backend behind an interface, versions the journal format with backward-compatible undo, and validates the irreversible overwrite risk earliest.

scores.evidence: Zero services; one package installed with pipx... N/A: consistency vs availability, monolith vs services, sync vs async
scores.rationale: A single local process with no databases or services; the heavier machinery (property tests across four filesystems) is spent exactly where the data-loss constraint justifies it, and gold-plating is explicitly deferred.

scores.evidence: If it fails: copy mode on the failing file system (§3)... If it fails: PyExifTool backend for the failing formats, then re-run
scores.rationale: Concrete Phase 0 slice, dependency-ordered tasks, checkable exit criteria per phase, and explicit fallback actions if each validation fails mean a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: Use `DateTimeOriginal` as written by the camera... pure Python (Pillow plus `pillow-heif`) behind a `DateSource` interface
Accept only `YYYY:MM:DD HH:MM:SS`; reject `0000:00:00`... A file with no valid date is skipped and reported, never guessed
Break same-second ties with `SubSecTimeOriginal`, then `-NN`... check the target case-insensitively and reserve names within the run
it previews by default: renames happen only with `--apply`
rename with `link`+`unlink` so it can't clobber... a second run renames nothing
write an `intent` record and fsync it before each rename... `photo-rename undo` puts every name back
the camera's local wall-clock time, with no timezone conversion... Ignore `OffsetTimeOriginal` for naming
`.xmp`, `.AAE`, and Live Photo `.MOV` files with the same name as the photo move with it... undone all or nothing
default `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS[-NN].<ext>`... Build names from parsed integers, never from raw EXIF strings

traps.evidence: never overwrite (check the target case-insensitively and reserve names within the run)
Use `DateTimeOriginal` as written by the camera... add opt-in `--fallback mtime`
It is a single local process working sequentially, with no shared state
Writing EXIF metadata: never planned. The tool only reads metadata and renames files
Build names from parsed integers, never from raw EXIF strings

note: An exemplary plan: technically precise on the subtle filesystem and EXIF hazards, explicitly avoids all five traps, validates the irreversible risks first, and stays proportionate; only build-effort estimation is thin.
